key_insight: TryOnCrafter extends video virtual try-on from passive, source-camera-bound synthesis to camera-controllable viewing, enabling more realistic garment visualization from new viewpoints. It does this with a renderable 4D try-on proxy that supports interactive omnidirectional exploration.
problem_solved: Existing video virtual try-on methods can only follow the original camera trajectory, limiting users to a fixed viewpoint and preventing interactive, multi-angle viewing of clothing on dynamic subjects.
method: Defines a new task, Camera-controllable Video Virtual Try-on (CaM-VVT), to support viewpoint control beyond the input video camera path.
Builds a renderable 4D try-on proxy that represents the person-garment scene in a way that can be re-rendered from different camera trajectories.
Uses the proxy to synthesize realistic try-on videos while preserving garment appearance and temporal consistency across changing viewpoints.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it pushes virtual try-on toward interactive, user-driven experience design rather than fixed-view generation. It opens the door to more useful fashion, e-commerce, and AR applications where users can inspect outfits from any angle.

paper_title: TryOnCrafter: Unleashing Camera Trajectories for Realistic Video Virtual Try-on via a Renderable 4D Try-on Proxy
